question: A 33-year-old African-American female presents to her physician with complaints of a persistent, dry cough. She states that the cough has gone on for some time now. Three weeks ago, during her last general checkup, she was started on lisinopril and metformin for concerns regarding an elevated blood pressure and fasting blood glucose. Past medical history is notable for eczema, asthma, and seasonal allergies. At this visit the patient has other non-specific complaints such as fatigue and joint pain as well as a burning sensation in her sternum when she eats large meals. Her physical exam is only notable for painful bumps on her lower extremities (figure A) which the patient attributes to "bumping her shins," during exercise, and an obese habitus. Which of the following is most likely true for this patient's chief concern?

options.opa: Serum levels of bradykinin will be elevated
options.opb: Loratadine would best treat her chief complaint
options.opc: Beta agonists would relieve this patients symptoms
options.opd: Non-caseating granulomas are found on biopsy of mediastinal lymph nodes
options.ope: Omeprazole is an appropriate next step in management

analysis: The patient's presentation is suggestive of sarcoidosis, given her symptoms of persistent dry cough, joint pain, fatigue, and the presence of painful bumps on her lower extremities (erythema nodosum). The burning sensation in her sternum when eating large meals could be indicative of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), which can be associated with sarcoidosis. Non-caseating granulomas are a hallmark finding in sarcoidosis, typically found on biopsy of affected tissues. Therefore, option 'opd. Non-caseating granulomas are found on biopsy of mediastinal lymph nodes' is the most likely true for this patient's chief concern.
